test_title: PYST 04: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question: Which among the following sentences uses the article (if required) before the word 'honour' correctly?

options.text: It is the honour to be here.
It is an honour to be here.
It is honour to be here.
It is a honour to be here.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. It is an honour to be here.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'honour'** begins with a silent 'h', which makes it phonetically start with a vowel sound ('onour').
 
• When a word starts with a vowel sound, the article **'an'** is used before it instead of 'a'.
 
• Option 2, **'It is an honour to be here,'** correctly follows this rule.

Correct sentence: *It is an honour to be here.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1:** 'the honour' is inappropriate here because 'the' is used for something specific or already mentioned.
 
• **Option 3: **'honour' without an article is grammatically incomplete.
 
• **Option 4:** 'a honour' is incorrect because 'a' cannot precede words with vowel sounds.
